pre_event_materials: Generic React starter kit written by the team before the event and committed as the repository's first commit, 'Starter kit baseline'. Vite + React 19 + Tailwind 4 shell (index.html, src/main.jsx, src/App.jsx, src/app.css), a localStorage/Supabase storage adapter (src/lib/db.js), a library of thirteen generic self-contained capability modules with their own tests (src/recipes/), five accessible colour palettes (src/themes/), and helper scripts (scripts/preflight.sh, scripts/smoke-live.sh, scripts/compress-video.sh). It contains no solution to P08 or to any other released problem; it was written before the problems were known. Declared in full in EVENT.md.
Documentation templates from the same starter kit: README-TEMPLATE.md, SUBMISSION-TEMPLATE.md, LICENSES.md, BOARD.md, DEPLOY.md, CLAUDE.md.

sample_data.method: seeded on start, plus file upload and paste
sample_data.reset_instructions: The published fixture case PUB-01 from P08_school_results_public.json is bundled at src/data/seed-p08.json and loads automatically on every page load, so the initial data is restored simply by reloading the page. Nothing is persisted to localStorage or to any server. To load a different case, paste its JSON object into the load box in the header or upload a file containing it.

problem_solving_method: The grading rules are the entire problem, so they were built as a pure module with a node --test suite written before any user interface, and the interface reads from it. The organizers' published fixture shape was adopted directly as the application's data model rather than designing a schema and mapping onto it, so an unpublished case in the same shape loads without a translation layer. Each of the four required items is owned by exactly one unit on its own branch and its own files, and each is verified on the deployed URL rather than locally before being called done.
major_design_decisions: The organizers' published fixture shape is the application's data model, rather than a schema of our own with a mapping layer, so that an unpublished case in the same shape loads unchanged.
The grading rules live in one pure module with a node --test suite written before the interface, because the rules are the problem and the interface is a view of them.
The GPA is rounded once at two decimal places and the letter grade is derived from that rounded value, so the letter and the number shown can never disagree at a band boundary.

A compulsory failure zeroes the GPA and sets the letter to F, but leaves every subject grade point and the uncancelled average populated, because clarification R-13 requires the uncancelled average to stay visible in the trace.

An absent subject and a subject scored zero are distinct values end to end: absent carries a null mark and renders as AB, zero renders as 0 with its own rule text, per the problem's explicit constraint that the two must not produce the same output.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Reading and reconciling the organizer documents, authoring the build specification in SPEC.md, and implementing units against that specification.
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: The grading rules are covered by a node --test suite exercising every grade-band boundary and each edge case named in the clarifications. Every required item was additionally checked by a team member on the deployed URL, not locally, before being recorded as done.

declaration: The information above is complete and truthful to the best of the team's knowledge.
